package proto

import (
	"errors"
	"runtime"
	"sync"
	"testing"
	"unsafe"
)

// growGo uses about depth*256 bytes of Go stack, forcing it to grow.
//
//go:noinline
func growGo(depth int) int {
	var pad [256]byte
	pad[depth%256] = byte(depth)
	if depth == 0 {
		return int(pad[0])
	}
	return growGo(depth-1) + int(pad[depth%256])
}

// frameAddr is the address of a local in the calling frame, as an integer:
// it changes exactly when the stack was copied.
//
//go:noinline
func frameAddr(x *int) uintptr { return uintptr(unsafe.Pointer(x)) }

// Item 2: the callee takes its parameters' addresses, changes the copies and
// writes the result, then Go moves its stack. The caller's object is
// unchanged and the result is complete.
func TestAddressTakenParams(t *testing.T) {
	vm := NewVM()
	defer vm.Close()
	moved := false
	vm.onCall = func(vm *VM, id, arg int64, sp uintptr) int64 {
		if id != cbGrow {
			t.Fatalf("unexpected callback %d", id)
		}
		var x int
		before := frameAddr(&x)
		growGo(4096) // about 1 MiB
		moved = frameAddr(&x) != before
		return 0
	}
	r, err := vm.Eval(func(sp uintptr) int64 { return addr_param(sp, 7, 40, 1.5) })
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("addr_param: %v (%d)", err, r)
	}
	if r != 1040+3 {
		t.Fatalf("addr_param = %d, want 1043", r)
	}
	if !moved {
		t.Fatal("the Go stack did not move during the callback")
	}
	if vm.top != vm.Empty() {
		t.Fatal("shadow stack not empty after return")
	}
}

// Item 3: the Go stack shrinks (and is copied) while a C frame with live
// state is below the callback.
func TestStackShrinkUnderCFrame(t *testing.T) {
	vm := NewVM()
	defer vm.Close()
	var grew, shrank bool
	vm.onCall = func(vm *VM, id, arg int64, sp uintptr) int64 {
		if id == cbObserve {
			return 0
		}
		var x int
		a0 := frameAddr(&x)
		growGo(8192) // about 2 MiB
		a1 := frameAddr(&x)
		grew = a1 != a0
		for i := 0; i < 4 && frameAddr(&x) == a1; i++ {
			runtime.GC()
		}
		shrank = frameAddr(&x) != a1
		return 5
	}
	done := make(chan struct{})
	var r int64
	var err error
	go func() { // a fresh goroutine, so its stack starts small
		defer close(done)
		r, err = vm.Eval(func(sp uintptr) int64 { return shrink_frame(sp, 3, 4) })
	}()
	<-done
	if err != nil || r != 3+4+7+12+5 {
		t.Fatalf("shrink_frame = %d, %v", r, err)
	}
	if !grew || !shrank {
		t.Fatalf("stack grew %v, shrank %v: both copies must happen", grew, shrank)
	}
}

// Item 4: enter from Go callers whose frames leave SP at both 16-byte
// remainders; the double and vector spills inside must still be right.
func TestFrameRemainders(t *testing.T) {
	want := vecSpillGo(1.5, 2.5)
	seen := map[uintptr]bool{}
	for _, call := range []func(a, b float64) (float64, uintptr){via0, via1, via2, via3, via4, via5} {
		got, sp := call(1.5, 2.5)
		seen[(sp-8)%16] = true
		if got != want {
			t.Fatalf("vec_spill = %v, want %v (entry SP %%16 = %d)", got, want, (sp-8)%16)
		}
	}
	if !seen[0] || !seen[8] {
		t.Fatalf("entry SP remainders seen: %v, need both 0 and 8", seen)
	}
}

func vecSpillGo(a, b float64) float64 {
	x0, x1 := a, b
	y0, y1 := b, a
	s := a * b
	k := 1.0
	x0, x1 = x0*y0+k, x1*y1+k
	y0, y1 = y0-x0, y1-x1
	k = 1
	return x0 + x1 + y0*y1 + s + k
}

func callerSP() uintptr

//go:noinline
func sinkBytes(p []byte) { p[0]++ }

//go:noinline
func via0(a, b float64) (float64, uintptr) { sp := callerSP(); return vec_spill(0, a, b), sp }

//go:noinline
func via1(a, b float64) (float64, uintptr) {
	var p [8]byte
	sinkBytes(p[:])
	sp := callerSP()
	return vec_spill(0, a, b) + float64(p[0]-1), sp
}

//go:noinline
func via2(a, b float64) (float64, uintptr) {
	var p [16]byte
	sinkBytes(p[:])
	sp := callerSP()
	return vec_spill(0, a, b) + float64(p[0]-1), sp
}

//go:noinline
func via3(a, b float64) (float64, uintptr) {
	var p [24]byte
	sinkBytes(p[:])
	sp := callerSP()
	return vec_spill(0, a, b) + float64(p[0]-1), sp
}

//go:noinline
func via4(a, b float64) (float64, uintptr) {
	var p [40]byte
	sinkBytes(p[:])
	sp := callerSP()
	return vec_spill(0, a, b) + float64(p[0]-1), sp
}

//go:noinline
func via5(a, b float64) (float64, uintptr) {
	var p [48]byte
	sinkBytes(p[:])
	sp := callerSP()
	return vec_spill(0, a, b) + float64(p[0]-1), sp
}

// Item 5: two levels of reentry into the same VM, with GC and a Go stack
// move at the innermost callback, ended by a normal return, a panic or a
// Goexit. Every level's fixed and dynamic locals keep their sentinels, the
// live areas do not overlap, and each record of the shadow position comes
// back when its callback ends.
func TestReentryMatrix(t *testing.T) {
	for _, mode := range []string{"return", "panic", "goexit"} {
		t.Run(mode, func(t *testing.T) {
			vm := NewVM()
			defer vm.Close()
			type level struct{ fixed, dynLo, dynHi, handoff uintptr }
			var levels []level
			var logs []uintptr
			var fail string
			vm.onCall = func(vm *VM, id, arg int64, sp uintptr) int64 {
				switch id {
				case cbObserve:
					return 0
				case cbLog:
					logs = append(logs, uintptr(arg))
					return 0
				case cbReenter:
					n := len(logs)
					levels = append(levels, level{logs[n-3], logs[n-2], logs[n-1], sp})
					if vm.top != sp {
						fail = "the bridge did not record the handoff"
					}
					if arg < 3 {
						r, err := vm.Eval(func(sp2 uintptr) int64 {
							if sp2 != sp {
								fail = "the reentry did not start at the handoff"
							}
							return reenter(sp2, arg+1, 16+arg)
						})
						if err != nil {
							fail = "inner eval: " + err.Error()
						}
						if vm.top != sp {
							fail = "the handoff record was not restored after the reentry"
						}
						return r
					}
					runtime.GC()
					growGo(4096)
					runtime.GC()
					switch mode {
					case "panic":
						panic("boom")
					case "goexit":
						runtime.Goexit()
					}
					return 0
				}
				fail = "unexpected callback"
				return 0
			}
			var r int64
			var err error
			var recovered any
			var wg sync.WaitGroup
			wg.Add(1)
			go func() {
				defer wg.Done()
				defer func() { recovered = recover() }()
				r, err = vm.Eval(func(sp uintptr) int64 { return reenter(sp, 1, 16) })
			}()
			wg.Wait()
			if fail != "" {
				t.Fatal(fail)
			}
			if len(levels) != 3 {
				t.Fatalf("reached %d levels, want 3", len(levels))
			}
			for i, l := range levels {
				if !(l.fixed < l.dynLo && l.dynLo < l.dynHi && l.dynHi <= l.handoff) {
					t.Fatalf("level %d: fixed %#x dyn [%#x,%#x) handoff %#x out of order", i+1, l.fixed, l.dynLo, l.dynHi, l.handoff)
				}
				if l.fixed < vm.Empty() || l.handoff >= vm.base+shadowSize-shadowGuard {
					t.Fatalf("level %d outside the shadow region", i+1)
				}
				if i > 0 && l.fixed < levels[i-1].handoff {
					t.Fatalf("level %d overlaps level %d", i+1, i)
				}
			}
			if vm.top != vm.Empty() {
				t.Fatal("outermost record not restored")
			}
			switch mode {
			case "return":
				if err != nil || r != 3+2+1 {
					t.Fatalf("reenter = %d, %v", r, err)
				}
				if vm.broken {
					t.Fatal("VM marked broken after a normal return")
				}
				if _, err := vm.Eval(func(sp uintptr) int64 { return deep(sp, 10) }); err != nil {
					t.Fatalf("VM unusable after the matrix: %v", err)
				}
			case "panic":
				if recovered != "boom" {
					t.Fatalf("recovered %v", recovered)
				}
				fallthrough
			case "goexit":
				if !vm.broken {
					t.Fatal("VM not marked broken")
				}
				if _, err := vm.Eval(func(sp uintptr) int64 { return deep(sp, 10) }); !errors.Is(err, ErrBroken) {
					t.Fatalf("Eval on a broken VM: %v", err)
				}
			}
		})
	}
}

// Item 6: an interrupt requested in the middle of a fragment that cannot
// fail lets the fragment finish, then propagates. The callback ignores the
// inner error and evaluates again: that must fail too, and so must the
// outer loop.
func TestInterruptPersists(t *testing.T) {
	vm := NewVM()
	defer vm.Close()
	const n = 50_000
	var inner []error
	var done []int64
	rounds := 0
	vm.onCall = func(vm *VM, id, arg int64, sp uintptr) int64 {
		if id != cbInnerEval {
			return 0
		}
		rounds++
		first := vm.polls.Load()
		vm.pollHook = func(k int64) {
			if k == first+5 {
				vm.Interrupt()
			}
		}
		for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
			_, err := vm.Eval(func(sp uintptr) int64 { return fragment(sp, vm.Slot(0), n, vm.Slot(1+i)) })
			inner = append(inner, err) // ignored on purpose
			done = append(done, vm.Word(1+i))
		}
		return 0
	}
	_, err := vm.Eval(func(sp uintptr) int64 { return outer_loop(sp, vm.Slot(0), 1000) })
	if !errors.Is(err, ErrInterrupted) {
		t.Fatalf("outer loop: %v, want interrupted", err)
	}
	if rounds != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("outer loop ran %d rounds after the interrupt, want 1", rounds)
	}
	for i := range inner {
		if !errors.Is(inner[i], ErrInterrupted) {
			t.Fatalf("inner eval %d: %v, want interrupted", i, inner[i])
		}
		if done[i] != n {
			t.Fatalf("fragment %d stopped at %d of %d", i, done[i], n)
		}
	}
	// The next outermost entry starts clean.
	if r, err := vm.Eval(func(sp uintptr) int64 { return fragment(sp, vm.Slot(0), 10, vm.Slot(1)) }); err != nil || r != 45 {
		t.Fatalf("fresh entry: %d, %v", r, err)
	}
}

// Item 7: running out of shadow stack raises RangeError, through deep
// recursion and through one large dynamic alloca, and the VM stays usable.
func TestShadowOverflow(t *testing.T) {
	vm := NewVM()
	defer vm.Close()
	vm.onCall = func(vm *VM, id, arg int64, sp uintptr) int64 { return 0 }
	var re *RangeError
	if _, err := vm.Eval(func(sp uintptr) int64 { return deep(sp, 1_000_000) }); !errors.As(err, &re) {
		t.Fatalf("deep recursion: %v, want RangeError", err)
	}
	if vm.top != vm.Empty() {
		t.Fatal("shadow stack not empty after the error")
	}
	if r, err := vm.Eval(func(sp uintptr) int64 { return deep(sp, 100) }); err != nil || r != 31 {
		t.Fatalf("deep(100) after overflow = %d, %v", r, err)
	}
	if _, err := vm.Eval(func(sp uintptr) int64 { return dyn_alloc(sp, 2<<20) }); !errors.As(err, &re) {
		t.Fatalf("dynamic alloca: %v, want RangeError", err)
	}
	if r, err := vm.Eval(func(sp uintptr) int64 { return dyn_alloc(sp, 512<<10) }); err != nil || r != 512<<10 {
		t.Fatalf("dyn_alloc(512K) = %d, %v", r, err)
	}
}
